custody.note: Exact video ID and private pack member hashes were verified. The installed v1.0 tool does not produce the newer canonical pack format.

overview: A critique of two studies in which an AI revises the procedures used by another agent and the role of evaluation in that loop.
whyItMatters: Research benchmarks can justify a scoped experiment, but not a general production claim.
ghostMeshTakeaway: Specify a grader and holdout before allowing a harness to adapt.

normalization.overview: Cloud Codes compares two research efforts that let an AI system revise its own working procedure, then argues that evaluation design determines whether this feedback helps.
normalization.whyItMatters: Useful for teams tempted to treat an adaptive agent harness as a reusable product recipe. The reported gains are real author results on specified tasks, while coding transfer is mixed.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Treat a proposed harness change as an experiment with a named grader, held-out tasks and a rollback path. Do not promote a self-judged gain into production authority.
normalization.falsification: Revisit the cautious call if independent held-out coding and operational tasks show reliable gains with recorded failures, cost, authority constraints and external grading; abandon a candidate if it only improves its own proxy score.
normalization.freshness: Publisher video, private caption aids and direct paper versions checked 2026-10-20. Benchmarks and product behavior can change; the two studies are not independent confirmations of the same outcome.

claims.proposition: Harness learning revises executable agent orchestration from task feedback while model weights stay fixed during test-time adaptation.
claims.assessment: The authors define a proposer that edits a frozen solver harness and train it with execution feedback.
claims.limits: Corroborates the reported design, not safe self-modification in an open production environment.
claims.temporalScope: Video and paper versions checked 2026-10-20; study outcomes are specific to their reported protocols.

claims.proposition: In the paper’s 21 unseen Reasoning Gym families, a trained 4B proposer averages 0.62 for one revision versus 0.56 for its 35B teacher under the same protocol.
claims.assessment: The author paper reports the comparison and a base proposer mean of 0.32.
claims.limits: The teacher does better under oracle best-of-eight selection. These are bounded puzzle scores, not coding reliability or a general model ranking.
claims.temporalScope: Video and paper versions checked 2026-10-20; study outcomes are specific to their reported protocols.

claims.proposition: MASS uses a single base model in distinct solver, optimizer and evaluator roles, then alternates workflow search with training on generated trajectories.
claims.assessment: The author paper specifies the role loop and two rounds using Qwen3.6-27B.
claims.limits: The evaluator is part of the same model family; this is not independent external grading.
claims.temporalScope: Video and paper versions checked 2026-10-20; study outcomes are specific to their reported protocols.

claims.proposition: After two MASS rounds, score per output token rises 1.20 to 1.60 times baseline on four research benchmarks but is 0.96 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 0.94 on SWE-bench Verified.
claims.assessment: The research team reports these ratios for the stated benchmark set.
claims.limits: The coding ratios are below baseline and the team notes uneven transfer. Neither ratio predicts a GhostMesh workflow result.
claims.temporalScope: Video and paper versions checked 2026-10-20; study outcomes are specific to their reported protocols.

claims.proposition: Better agent scaffolding by itself makes an agent trustworthy on new work.
claims.assessment: The video itself argues that a weak grader can optimize the wrong target; the two papers measure particular tasks and feedback loops.
claims.limits: A production decision needs holdout tasks, authority boundaries, cost and failure checks, with independent verification of important actions.
claims.temporalScope: Video and paper versions checked 2026-10-20; study outcomes are specific to their reported protocols.

relationships.reason: Both ask how an agent result becomes inspectable. This Reader examines feedback used to change a harness; the earlier Reader asks for visible work and a reviewable result. The earlier video does not validate the paper benchmarks.

Both consider evaluated research agents. This video highlights adaptive workflow optimization, while the paper Reader distinguishes a completed experiment from an advance in scientific knowledge. Shared interest is not independent replication.
